cells.tense: You are standing where the load is heaviest, and you are still standing whole.
cells.ask: Say out loud what you're protecting, and name the one thing you're dropping so it keeps standing.
cells.core:
Someone watching would notice how much you carry without calling it heavy. The gathering is working. What was scattered is collected and pointed at the one thing that matters, and that thing has a name even if you haven't said it lately. Enduring isn't the same as waiting something out. You hold without going stiff, and people can still reach you while you hold.

This is a good place to be, not a rest stop. When the pressure eases, the pull will be to fold straight into the next load, so use the good stretch instead. Say what you're protecting, plainly, once. Name one thing you're carrying only out of habit and set it down. That keeps the balance from quietly turning back into bracing. Standing steady is worth spending a little on purpose, not just holding until the next thing arrives.

cells.verb: Gathering what was scattered and holding it at the one point that matters
cells.place: Endurance under pressure, holding a form that hasn't broken

cells.tense: You are bracing for a fight that has not arrived, and your body is already in it.
cells.ask: Set the coming hour aside for one day. Ask one plain question about how this stands right now.
cells.core:
You're dug in against something that hasn't fully shown up. Maybe the argument, the setback, the next thing that will need defending — you've already gone tense in that direction. It checks out as grit, and it looks like grit. But grit aimed at a threat that isn't here is just a body on alert. Being dug in has become the whole thing, and whatever you were originally standing for has gone quiet underneath it.

What you're actually after is a direction that comes from somewhere alive in you, not from what you expect to have to resist. That's still in there, just drowned out by preparation. Put down what's coming and ask one plain question about this hour. See whether the ground holds without you pressing on it. Often it does, and you find you were bracing against your own weight.

cells.tense: You stopped asking anything of yourself a long time ago, and that door is behind you now.
cells.ask: Pick one small thing that is plainly yours and stand behind it for an afternoon.
cells.core:
There's a direction you chose once, and you're nowhere near it now. You kept showing up, you didn't break — but it got separated from whatever it was for. So it turned quiet and mechanical, or it went the other way and you let go early, and the story became that nothing was worth standing behind long enough.

Either way the strength itself isn't gone. There's just nothing live flowing into it. Don't try to push feeling back in. Start lower and smaller: one thing that is plainly yours and plainly small, and one afternoon behind it. If the ground holds, the reason behind the standing comes back on its own, and wanting comes with it. The afternoon is only the first thing you can point at, and pointing at something is enough.
cells.sheetLine: You kept carrying. You just stopped asking it for anything.

cells.tense: You are holding the line already, and you talk about it as though it happened on its own.
cells.ask: Say out loud, once, that you are the one holding this.
cells.core:
You are already the one steadying things — how they move, what stays standing, where the weight lands. It happens whether or not anyone names it. But the way you describe it keeps sliding into the passive, as if the evenness belonged to the room and not to you. Staying upright is real. Somewhere along the way, you stopped being the one who does it.

What's missing is smaller and plainer than getting credit: this is mine, you're the one doing it. That's not a boast. It's being the author of something you're already writing. Once you can say it out loud, you don't hold less. You get to choose what to hold. That's the difference between keeping a line and being kept by it. Say it once without the usual hedge, and notice what moves.
